findings.title: `queued` is a datetime that gets passed through Celery task kwargs, which are likely not JSON-serializable
findings.body: `AssignmentSource.to_dict()` returns `asdict(self)`, which includes the `queued` datetime object as-is. `sync_group_assignee_outbound` puts this dict into `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(kwargs=...)` as `assignment_source_dict`. If the integrations task queue serializes arguments as JSON (the usual Celery setup in Sentry), the datetime makes `apply_async` fail with a serialization error. The outbound assignee sync would then break for every assignment that carries a source, which is the exact webhook path this PR is meant to fix. The tests only call `to_dict()` directly and never push the result through a task, so this is not caught. Either serialize `queued` to an ISO string in `to_dict` and parse it back in `from_dict`, or drop the field from the serialized payload.

findings.title: Default `queued` timestamp is evaluated once at import time
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a dataclass default, so it is computed once when the module is imported. Every `AssignmentSource` created in the process then gets the same stale timestamp, not the time the assignment happened. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead.

findings.title: `should_sync` is now called with two arguments on all installations, which breaks overrides that accept only one
findings.body: The task now calls `installation.should_sync("outbound_assignee", parsed_assignment_source)`. `IssueBasicIntegration.should_sync` was updated, but any installation whose class overrides `should_sync(self, attribute)` with the old one-argument signature will raise TypeError at runtime. The outbound sync path is then broken for that integration. Either update all overrides in the same PR or only pass the source when the method accepts it.
